name: Settling and Force Reporting in Free Surface Flow
goal: Establish how to decide when a free-surface experiment or simulation has settled, reached a statistically stationary or quasi-steady regime, or remains genuinely transient, and how forces should be reported in each case. PRIORITISE TRANSFERABILITY OF THE CRITERION OR PROTOCOL OVER TRANSFERABILITY OF QUOTED NUMERICAL TIMES. Three tagged sub-problems: decay to stationarity for a fixed body; a defensible force statistic during a finite-duration moving-body passage; and a threshold-crossing decision from a noisy record. PRESERVE THE DISTINCTION BETWEEN A CRITERION AND ITS NUMERICAL PARAMETER. Include a separate numerical reproducibility thread on non-deterministic atomic accumulation in particle-to-grid operations, non-associative floating-point addition, and order-dependent GPU reductions. The motivating observation is that three nominally identical runs produced final settling velocities of 0.865234, 0.861557 and 0.594807 with identical peaks to four decimals; two failed the settling gate and one passed at 974 frames.
summary:
NO UNIVERSAL FRAME COUNT OR FORCE-SETTLING THRESHOLD EMERGES: the defensible protocol is to detect and exclude initial and final transients, demonstrate stationarity for the reported observable, and attach uncertainty based on correlated samples [Bro19, Ber21d, Lon05].

[1] DECAY TO STATIONARITY. Fixed-body and disturbed-free-surface studies support OBSERVABLE-SPECIFIC gates, energy/damping decay, stable mean and bandwidth, or automated truncation, NOT universal times [Sch85, He24d, Puj24, Cho15, Oli24]. Autocorrelation, integrated correlation time, blocking and bootstrap convert a stationary record into an effective sample size [Fly89, Gro18, Jon18, Dur20]. Tank practice waits for measured residual-wave levels, with the first sloshing mode governing inter-run offset time [Jen21, Tho07].

[2] FINITE-DURATION MOVING PASSAGES. For ship resistance, report a PRESPECIFIED constant-speed interior window, its mean, filter and window sensitivity, and correlated uncertainty [Cal80, Doc08, Ste15, Bro19]. This is a protocol, not a transferable run length. SLAMMING, WATER ENTRY AND IMPACT LOADING GENERALLY HAVE NO STEADY FORCE: report peak distributions, impulses, envelopes or event statistics with repeat-run uncertainty. Evidence for a universally accepted moving-body settling criterion remains thin.

[3] THRESHOLD DECISIONS. Incipient motion is PROBABILISTIC AND RECORD-LENGTH DEPENDENT; define a movement probability or activity rate with detection uncertainty, not a single critical stress [Lav87, Nei69, Dan02, Dip10].

NUMERICAL REPRODUCIBILITY. Non-associative, order-dependent reductions can produce small drift OR ALTER DISCRETE GATES; fixed-order or sorted reproducible reductions and higher-precision accumulation mitigate this [Xu19b, Ahr15, Sik24]. Repeated runs should report outcome spread and gate-pass frequency; NO UNIVERSAL REPEAT COUNT EXISTS, and independent-start ensembles are the stronger convergence check [Sto18b, Wie11, Zha23].
